claim: The cyclic groups C_r and C_(r+1) have no common nontrivial quotient, so a construction requiring the same nontrivial one-step image for both row cycles cannot work.
quantifiers: For every integer r>=1, the order of any common quotient of C_r and C_(r+1) divides gcd(r,r+1).
proof: A quotient of C_r has order dividing r; a quotient of C_(r+1) has order dividing r+1. A common quotient's order divides both and therefore divides their gcd 1.

costs.scope: This only excludes a common nontrivial quotient of the adjacent row-coordinate groups; different images inside a larger group, second-coordinate maps, and non-homomorphic colorings remain possible.

strongest_baseline: The Cycle 6 aligned constructions use a shared nontrivial coordinate quotient; this identifies why the first-coordinate-only version cannot directly pass across both adjacent N65 row moduli.
falsifier: A common nontrivial quotient of C_r and C_(r+1).
scope: It does not exclude different coordinate images in a larger group, use of second coordinates, non-homomorphic colorings, noncommuting matrices, or other representations.

claim: For an arbitrary overlapping family of p-by-p triangle blocks, where p is odd prime and one global F_p color agrees with either block coordinate up to a blockwise offset, a scalar-matrix assignment over any coefficient field containing a primitive p-th root satisfies every triangle and makes every nondegenerate rectangle I-W invertible in every matrix dimension D.
quantifiers: For every odd prime p, field F with zeta in F of exact order p, D>=1, finite label set I, finite family B with |I_b|=p^2 and bijections phi_b:I_b->F_p^2, and epsilon:I->F_p such that for every b there are c_b in F_p and o_b in {alpha_b,beta_b} with epsilon(i)=o_b(i)+c_b for all i in I_b.
proof: Set X_iuv=zeta^((epsilon(i)+u+v)^2)I_D. If alpha-oriented, set L^b_{u,j}=zeta^(-(j+c_b+u)^2)I_D and R=I_D; if beta-oriented, set L=I_D and R^b_{v,k}=zeta^((k+c_b+v)^2)I_D. Substitution in LXR^-1=I_D is exact. A rectangle exponent is 2(u'-u)(v'-v), which is nonzero in F_p for distinct rows and columns because p is odd; zeta has order p, so I-W is invertible.

costs.symbolic_storage: O(|I|+|B|) color/orientation data beyond supplied coordinates; materializing matrices costs O((|I|+|B|)p^2D^2) entries.
costs.field_requirement: F must contain a primitive p-th root; a finite extension of any prime field of characteristic ell!=p with degree ord_p(ell) suffices.
costs.arithmetic: Precomputing powers of zeta costs O(p) field multiplications; then each variable uses O(1) lookups and field operations. No oracle or approximation.

strongest_baseline: The prior Cycle 5 result gives explicit two-block solutions and the binary Cycle 6 theorem handles arbitrary overlapping 2x2 blocks. This extends the aligned construction to p-by-p blocks for every odd p.
falsifier: Any failed triangle substitution, a rectangle with exponent 0 for distinct u,u' and v,v', or a coefficient-field element zeta asserted to have order p but not satisfying that order.

claim: For an arbitrary overlapping family of binary 2x2 triangle blocks admitting a common color epsilon that is, on each block, one coordinate up to a blockwise flip, there is an exact scalar-matrix assignment over every field with more than three elements such that all triangle equations hold and every nondegenerate rectangle has I-W invertible, in every matrix dimension D.
quantifiers: For every field F with |F|>3, every D>=1, every finite label set I, every finite family B with four-label subsets I_b and bijections phi_b:I_b->F_2^2, and every epsilon:I->F_2 such that for each b there are c_b in F_2 and o_b in {alpha_b,beta_b} with epsilon(i)=o_b(i)+c_b for all i in I_b.
proof: Choose t in F* with t^2!=1. Set X_iuv=t^-1 I_D iff epsilon(i)+u+v=0, otherwise I_D. If epsilon=alpha_b+c_b, set L^b_{u,j}=tI_D iff u+j+c_b=0 and R^b=I_D; if epsilon=beta_b+c_b, set L^b=I_D and R^b_{v,k}=t^-1I_D iff v+k+c_b=0. Substitution proves LXR^-1=I_D for every shared triangle. The canonical 2x2 rectangle is t^-2I_D for epsilon=0 and t^2I_D for epsilon=1; any ordering is one of these or its inverse. Hence I-W is a nonzero scalar multiple of I_D.

costs.parameter_search: At most three nonzero field elements need be tested to find t because X^2-1 has at most two roots.
costs.symbolic_storage: O(|I|+|B|) labels and orientation bits; materializing D-by-D scalar matrices costs O((|I|+|B|)D^2) entries.
costs.arithmetic: One field inverse t^-1 and constant-time scalar decisions per variable; no approximation or oracle.

strongest_baseline: A one-block full-rank local construction and a specific two-block identity/transpose construction were independently established in the Cycle 5 leaves. This theorem extends those examples to arbitrary overlaps under the explicit common-coordinate condition and all fields of size greater than three.
falsifier: A failed triangle substitution, a rectangle scalar equal to 1 despite t^2!=1, or a source-legal full-coordinate assignment satisfying the theorem's coloring hypothesis while contradicting the resulting finite GL assignment.
scope: Applies to 2x2 blocks whose coordinates lie in F_2. It is not an assignment for the larger N65 incidence system, whose actual coordinate maps have not been shown to satisfy the common-color condition. It does not alter the candidate N65 nonsoficity claim or establish linear soficity.

claim: If an exact finite presentation and rectangle list admit one globally compatible binary or odd-prime alignment theorem instance over a finite coefficient field, then the explicit edge assignment induces a homomorphism to a finite sofic group separating every listed rectangle; this would contradict the N65 finite-permutation obstruction if all its premises and its rectangle list are valid.
quantifiers: Conditional on either (i) a complete binary aligned 2x2 block family over one finite field of size greater than three, or (ii) a complete p-by-p aligned family for one odd prime p over one finite field containing a primitive p-th root; every triangle and every required rectangle must be included.
proof: The appropriate construction satisfies all triangle relators and maps every listed rectangle W to a matrix different from I_D. For finite F, GL_D(F) is finite, so this defines a homomorphism into a finite, hence sofic, group that preserves the full rectangle list. The N65 obstruction says no such sofic-target map exists if its premises hold.

costs.certificate_check: Linear-time verification in the number of block-label incidences once the coordinate tables are supplied.
costs.finite_target: |GL_D(F)| is finite; no size optimization is claimed.

strongest_baseline: The N65 source-derived obstruction already rules out a finite sofic target preserving all rectangle words; this gives a concrete algebraic certificate whose existence would contradict that obstruction.
falsifier: An actual full N65 coordinate list satisfying the alignment condition but failing one formula, or a valid N65 proof whose rectangle set is not the complete set preserved by the assignment.
